title: Should Homework Be Banned?
text:
Many people believe that homework should be banned in primary schools. In my opinion, this view is partly correct, although the reasons are not always the ones people give. Young children need time to play, rest, and spend time with their families. However, a small amount of regular practice can help them build reading and maths skills. Therefore, I think schools should limit homework rather than abolish it completely.

The main argument against homework is that it creates unnecessary stress. Some teachers, however, argue that homework teaches responsibility and time management. Both points deserve attention. A reasonable compromise would be short tasks that take no more than twenty minutes a day. This approach respects children's free time while still reinforcing what they learn in class.

questions.text: According to the writer, what do young children need?
options: Time to play, rest and spend time with family

questions.text: What does the writer suggest as a reasonable compromise?
options: Short tasks of no more than twenty minutes a day
Twice as much homework each week

questions.text: What can be inferred about the writer's position on homework?
options: Homework should be removed from schools entirely
Homework should be limited rather than banned

questions.text: Why does the writer mention the teachers' argument in the second paragraph?
options: To show the writer has no clear opinion
To present a counterpoint the writer takes seriously
To prove that homework is always harmful
To suggest that teachers are usually wrong

an agreement in which each side accepts less than it wanted

paragraph_translations: Muitas pessoas acreditam que o dever de casa deveria ser proibido nos anos iniciais do ensino fundamental. Na minha opinião, esse ponto de vista está parcialmente correto, embora as razões nem sempre sejam as que as pessoas apresentam. Crianças pequenas precisam de tempo para brincar, descansar e passar tempo com suas famílias. No entanto, uma pequena quantidade de prática regular pode ajudá-las a desenvolver habilidades de leitura e matemática. Portanto, acredito que as escolas deveriam limitar o dever de casa em vez de aboli-lo completamente.

O principal argumento contra o dever de casa é que ele cria estresse desnecessário. Alguns professores, porém, defendem que o dever de casa ensina responsabilidade e gestão do tempo. Os dois pontos merecem atenção. Um meio-termo razoável seria tarefas curtas, que não tomem mais de vinte minutos por dia. Essa abordagem respeita o tempo livre das crianças e, ao mesmo tempo, reforça o que elas aprendem em sala de aula.
